**Finding: deviation (high severity) — Section 6.1 (¶ p0037)**

Contrary to the planner's "likely absent" hint, the agreement does contain a restrictive covenant binding us. Section 6.1 bars the Company, during the term, from participating in *any* similar Internet project involving Deerskin Products "or products substantially similar to Deerskin Products," expressly including third-party competitor lines (Wilson's House of Leather, Excelled, and "companies similar" to them) — an undefined field-of-use restriction on what we may source, build or sell, with no carve-out for internal development or acquisitions.

Notes on direction and proportionality:
- Section 6.3 (two-year post-term restriction on HDI) binds the vendor and was left untouched.
- Section 6.2 (closeout-merchandise site) is a limited existing carve-out benefiting us.
- Because HDI bears all Site development and hosting costs and the "Deerskin"-brand exclusivity is the core bargain, I took the **fallback** rather than deleting the covenant: the restriction is confined to a self-contained "Deerskin"-branded consumer web site, stays term-only (Section 4.1 — one year, annual renewals, 90 days' notice, so no post-term tail), and gains carve-outs for other channels, internal development and acquired businesses.

Redline validated (ok:true) and finding submitted with the [Playbook]-prefixed comment offering deletion as our preferred position.
